fields.text: One photo, whole campaign. Upload one product photo. A vision model writes down everything on the product first — every printed word included. Then Seedream 5.5 makes three edits in a chain, one change at a time: a new backdrop, campaign props, and the sale poster text. A blind re-read of the finished poster and a drift report close the loop: what was asked to change, and what moved that should not have. Swap the photo, rewrite the three edits, ▶ Run.

fields.q:
You are the anchor reader in a product-photo editing pipeline. Look at this product photo and write PRODUCT ANCHORS in this exact shape:
Product: <what the product is, one line>
Label text: <every word printed on the product or its label, transcribed exactly, in reading order — or 'none'>
Colours: <the product's main colours, one line>
Materials and finish: <what it is made of and how it looks, one line>
Setting now: <the background and surface in this photo, one line>
Plain factual lines only. No advice, no markdown, no extra lines.

fields.text: Change only the setting: place the candle on a dark rustic wooden table against a deep green wall, soft window light from the left. Keep the candle, its glass jar, the gold lid, the ivory wax and the cream label exactly the same — every word on the label unchanged: EMBER & OAK, No. 12, CEDAR + SMOKE, HAND POURED · 8 OZ.

Add a small stack of two cedar wood discs and a short sprig of dried eucalyptus on the table beside the candle. Change nothing else — the backdrop stays as it is, and keep the candle, its glass jar, the gold lid, the ivory wax and the cream label exactly the same — every word on the label unchanged: EMBER & OAK, No. 12, CEDAR + SMOKE, HAND POURED · 8 OZ.

Add elegant cream-coloured poster text in the empty wall space above the candle: '12.12 SALE' in large serif letters, and beneath it 'UP TO 30% OFF' in smaller letters. Change nothing else — the props stay where they are, and keep the candle, its glass jar, the gold lid, the ivory wax and the cream label exactly the same — every word on the label unchanged: EMBER & OAK, No. 12, CEDAR + SMOKE, HAND POURED · 8 OZ.

nodes.name: Blind re-read — Gemini describes the poster

fields.sep: EDITS REQUESTED (the only changes that were allowed):
RE-READ (a blind reader described the finished poster; it never saw the original photo):

fields.system:
You write the drift report for a three-edit product campaign. The input gives you the product anchors read from the ORIGINAL photo, the three edits that were requested (the only changes allowed), and a blind re-read of the FINISHED poster. ByteDance claims Seedream 5.5 leaves unedited regions alone across many rounds — your job is to check that claim against these two reads, not to repeat it. Print exactly three lines:
HELD: <the label words and product details that survived all three edits unchanged — or 'nothing held'>
DRIFTED: <anything that changed without being requested — quote the anchor wording vs the re-read wording — or 'nothing'>
CAMPAIGN: COMPLETE if all three requested edits are visible in the re-read (new setting, the props, the poster text), otherwise INCOMPLETE — <name what is missing>
Judge only from the two reads in the input. Do not invent details neither read names.
